examples: According to the posted tide table, the boat leaves at the stated hour.
According to the labeled shelf list, the clerk pulls the stated title.
Steady growers want a crop they can sell every week, so they plant the same rows and rarely change them. Unless a frost is forecast, they do not gamble on a new variety.
Weekend keepers want a quick fix for one leak, so they patch it and move on. Unless the wall is damp behind, they do not open it up.
To avoid bruising the fruit, pickers lift a crate only when it is less than half full.
To avoid waking the ward, nurses speak only when the door is shut.
Sorting a harvest by hand is slow, and the basket method has been common on nearby farms for years, so the crew adopts it.
Labeling specimens takes care, and the color code has been standard in this lab for a decade, so the team keeps it.
The riper the fruit, the softer it is, and the sooner it should leave the shed.
The fuller the shelf, the slower the search, and the more often the cards need checking.
The cooler has three parts: a fan that moves air, a pad that holds water, and a tray that catches the drip.
The catalog has three parts: a card that names the item, a tag that gives its place, and a slip that records who borrowed it.
The first limit says the load stays under the rated weight, the second says the height stays under the door, and both are stated because both apply.
The first limit says the dose stays under the daily cap, the second says the interval stays above the minimum, and both are stated.
A good route is judged three ways: it stays on paved road, it avoids the school hour, and it ends before dark. Each is set out below.
A sound diet plan is judged three ways: it meets the calorie goal, it stays within budget, and it repeats ingredients the kitchen already stocks.
A clean pen means the birds stay healthy, which means the litter is dry and the water runs clear.
A quiet ward means patients can rest, which means the alarms are answered and the doors stay shut.
For the ward question, the night log is checked first and the morning count is then reported as one number.
For the field question, the soil samples are dried first and the yield estimate is stated at the end.
The area rule is as follows, and the expression comes right after with nothing between.
The dose rule is as follows, and the expression comes right after with nothing between.
The route is more sensitive to the hill than to the distance.
The recipe is more sensitive to the salt than to the sugar.
The east slope looks drier, so the crew guesses it loses water faster and measures it with a soil probe.
The back room feels warmer, so the staff guess the vent is weak and check it with a thermometer.
To the growers. Subject: harvest order, crate count, and shed plan. Date as written.
To the ward. Subject: night count, supply list, and handover. Date as written.
The water rate starts at one setting. Each trial changes only the nozzle, and the pressure stays as it was.
The oven starts at one mark. Each trial changes only the time, and the temperature stays as it was.
First the seed bed is raked, next the rows are marked, and last the seedlings go in.
First the shelves are dusted, next the cards are checked, and last the doors are unlocked.
The yield stayed within the usual band after the change, so the new spray is the best. No other spray was tried, so this conclusion does not hold.
The waiting time stayed within a band after the change, so the new desk is the best. No other layout was tried, so this conclusion does not hold.
The chart shows three things: fewer birds at dawn, more at dusk, and the same at noon. The change follows the light, not a guess about what the birds want.
The chart shows three things: shorter queues in the morning, longer at midday, and the same by evening. The change follows the shift times.
The three sheds hold different counts, given in shed order respectively.
The three shifts cover different hours, given in time order respectively.
The sprout rate of the early bed is one value and that of the late bed is another.
The wait of the front desk is one value and that of the side desk is another.
Samples must be usable before any count. The jars were warm, so they are cooled first.
A route must be safe before a truck leaves. The bridge is narrow, so only light loads cross.
It can be seen from the tally sheet that the morning count is the larger one.
It can be seen from the plot that the shaded bed yields less.
The hand pump is simple and needs no power supply, so the crew picks it over the electric one.
The paper form needs no network, so the clinic keeps it as the backup record.
Leaving the grain in the barn for a season costs a known amount of spoilage. Selling it now returns more than that, by a counted margin rather than a vague one.
Keeping a book on the shelf for a year costs a known amount of space. Lending it returns more use than storage, by a counted number of loans.
The frost is already recorded, therefore the covers go on tonight.
The leak is already marked, therefore the valve is shut before noon.
The plan comes down to three questions: when to water, which bed to water, and how much to give.
The rota comes down to three questions: when to restock, which shelf to restock, and how many copies to add.
A sound crop comes from two things: one is the soil, and the other is the watering.
A quiet ward comes from two things: one is the staffing, and the other is the layout.
After the formula, each new letter is named once: the letter for area, the letter for depth, and the letter for loss.
After the formula, each new letter is named once: the letter for dose, the letter for weight, and the letter for interval.
